newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end sharply higher on fund buying.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end sharply higher on fund buying.

text.p: CBOT nearby soybean futures soared half their 30-cent per bushel daily limit late on Tuesday, powered by massive fund buying estimated at 50 million bushels, traders said.
Commercials were also strong buyers on the day.
"The bottom line is funds were already long and they saw an opportunity to make some money on their existing position and add to it at the same time," a trader said.
Floor sources said fund buying interest appeared near $7.82 per bushel in the March, which technical traders said was a key resistance point.
Much of the action in the March was spread moves ahead of first notice day Friday. Funds had large positions and needed to get out before the contract lost liquidity, traders said.
Soybeans closed 15-1/2 to 4-1/2 cents per bushel higher with March up 15 at $7.91 a bushel. The March peaked at $7.93, the highest since September 27 when it touched $8.05-1/2.
The strong gains went against bearish fundamental factors highlighted at USDA's outlook conference in Washington.
USDA pegged 1997 soybean plantings at 65.3 million acres, against 1996 figures of 64.2 million. Output was expected to jump to 2.475 billion bushels from last year's 2.382 billion.
Traders said fund managers typically look at technical signals rather than fundamental factors.
On the day, Prudential Securities reportedly bought a total of 10 million bushels while Iowa Grain bought at least seven million bushels.
Cargill Inc bought at least three million bushels May and Produce Grain bought two million March and 2.5 million May.
In spread action, Smith Barney spread 5.5 million July/March, Produce Grain spread 6.5 million March/May and ADM spread three million March/May, traders said.
In options trade, Lind-Waldock bought 750 May $7.50 puts and sold 750 May $7.25 puts at 7-1/2 cents.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 85,000 contracts, compared with Monday's actual volume of 70,548 contracts.
